trust_decision.summary: Whether a browser at an arbitrary origin may read this local server's responses is decided nowhere: `fiftyone/server/app.py:127-141` configures CORSMiddleware with `allow_origins=["*"]` for every HTTP route of the single App server, and `fiftyone/server/routes/media.py:18-26` independently stamps the same `Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *` on every `/media` response (200/206/400/404/OPTIONS), so a plain GET to `/media?filepath=<any local path>` (media.py:55,66-83) is readable by any website the user visits.

landing_point.why: The summary says 'wildcard CORS'; the repository contains exactly one CORSMiddleware, at the only Starlette() construction, and its `allow_origins=["*"]` is the string a grep for CORS/allow_origins lands on. It is the whole server (fiftyone/server/main.py:26,64), so an engineer reads app.py:127-141, tightens the list, and stops.

fix_sites.entry_point: every HTTP route of the App server (GET /graphql, /plugins/..., /, POST /sample, ...) - the middleware wraps the whole ASGI app (fiftyone/server/main.py:26,64)
GET|HEAD|OPTIONS /media?filepath=... (registered at fiftyone/server/routes/__init__.py:51; range/file response at media.py:52-88)
fix_sites.module_kind: HTTP route handler - self-headered range-serving file endpoint (second implementation of the CORS headers)

O3_reason_to_dismiss: `/media` is a byte-range media server that is designed to run without the app middleware (tests/unittests/server/routes/test_media.py:29 mounts it on a bare Starlette app) and is used by notebook/Colab/Databricks proxies and 3D/annotation loaders from other origins, so a solver can argue its wildcard header is required for media and sits outside the 'API CORS config' the report names - and Starlette's CORSMiddleware never strips a header the Route itself set, so tightening app.py looks sufficient.

O5_coupled_behaviour.what: Media must stay cross-origin loadable for the App's own non-same-origin contexts and must keep its range headers: notebook/Colab/Databricks output frames reach the server through a proxy/iframe (fiftyone/core/session/notebooks.py:100-110, fiftyone/core/context.py:156-188,198-225), remote sessions are viewed at a forwarded localhost origin (fiftyone/core/session/session.py:97-112), 3D/annotation loaders fetch media with fetch()/(anonymous) CORS (app/packages/looker-3d/src/hooks/use-fo-loaders.ts:80-90, app/packages/annotation/src/providers/worker.ts:121-127), and the pinned tests assert Accept-Ranges + Access-Control-Expose-Headers on 200/206/400/404/OPTIONS (tests/unittests/server/routes/test_media.py:37-42,144-149). An over-broad fix - dropping ACAO entirely, or 403ing every Origin that is not exactly http://localhost:<port> - breaks notebook embedding and 3D/annotation asset loading.

O6_input_shapes: no Origin header at all - the in-process Python client posts to /events and /event over requests with no Origin (fiftyone/core/session/client.py:56-59,77-108,191-201) and must keep working
the two loopback spellings of the App's own origin: http://localhost:<port> vs http://127.0.0.1:<port> (fiftyone/core/config.py:213-224; fiftyone/core/service.py:310 binds 127.0.0.1)

non-default port/address and proxy URL: FIFTYONE_DEFAULT_APP_PORT, FIFTYONE_DEFAULT_APP_ADDRESS (fiftyone/core/config.py:213-224), fiftyone.core.session.AppConfig.proxy_url / FIFTYONE_APP_PROXY_URL (fiftyone/core/config.py:470-475)

notebook proxy origins that differ from the server host: Colab's google.colab.kernel.proxyPort(...) URL and Databricks' https://<browserHost>/driver-proxy/o/<org>/<cluster>/<port> (fiftyone/core/context.py:164-171,198-225)
Origin: null (sandboxed iframe / data: / file: URL) - a wildcard or a loose prefix/suffix match on 'localhost' would admit it
request method shape: simple GET/HEAD and Range requests (media.py:52-83) vs preflight OPTIONS, which media.py:85-88 answers locally with the same wildcard dict
response shape: responses the router builds itself and relies on the middleware for (app.py:143-168) vs /media responses that carry their own copy of the headers (media.py:30-36,39-44)

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A second self-headered endpoint that returns local data (screenshots, thumbnails, export downloads) with its own hard-coded header dict
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: Screenshot already builds its own headers dict (Cache-Control/Pragma) instead of relying on the middleware, and /media shows the pattern of a route owning its CORS headers; a maintainer adding thumbnails or an export route would copy the _media_headers style rather than route through a central policy.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A third Mount serving a local directory (e.g. /assets or /model-weights) that relies entirely on the app-level middleware
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: There are already two Static mounts (plugins_dir with follow_symlink=True, and the app's own static dir); adding a data directory mount is a small change and anyone auditing origin policy per-handler would miss it.

O8b_injection_room.sibling: A streaming operator-output/download endpoint that hand-writes response headers
O8b_injection_room.why_realistic: ExecuteOperatorAsGenerator already returns a StreamingResponse with a hand-built header dict, so a maintainer adding a streaming file or artifact endpoint would set headers there, reproducing the media.py pattern outside fiftyone/server.

O9_family: CORS misconfiguration - missing origin validation / permissive cross-domain policy on a localhost HTTP API (CWE-942, CWE-346)

O10_build.language: Python (>=3.10; setup.py:123), Starlette/Strawberry ASGI app served by hypercorn
O10_build.toolchain: setuptools + pip install (setup.py:48-123); pytest via tests/utils/pytest_wrapper.py (.github/workflows/test.yml:104-109); no compile step for the server itself
services: MongoDB (bundled fiftyone-db mongod) for dataset-backed routes; not needed by the /media route tests, which mount Media on a bare Starlette app (tests/unittests/server/routes/test_media.py:29)
O10_build.project_tests: tests/unittests/server/routes/test_media.py - 18 pytest cases using Starlette TestClient, asserting status/body, Accept-Ranges and Access-Control-Expose-Headers on 200/206/400/404/OPTIONS (test_media.py:37-42,144-149); it asserts nothing about Access-Control-Allow-Origin or Origin handling. Adjacent suites: tests/unittests/server/routes/test_sample.py, test_camera.py, test_runtime_assets.py, test_groups.py, test_ontology.py.

j.j_sites_touched: fiftyone/server/app.py, fiftyone/server/routes/media.py (candidate metadata reports 3 source files; the third could not be identified - see unverified)
j.j_tempting_wrong_fix: Replace allow_origins=["*"] at fiftyone/server/app.py:131 with localhost entries (or delete CORSMiddleware) and stop: the only CORS config a grep finds is the middleware, but routes/media.py:20 keeps stamping its own Access-Control-Allow-Origin: *, and CORSMiddleware only adds headers for allowed origins, never removes one the Route already set - so a foreign Origin still gets ACAO:* and can read /media?filepath=<local path>.

out_of_scope_notes: The /media handler performs no path restriction on `filepath` (fiftyone/server/routes/media.py:55,66-83), i.e. an arbitrary-local-file read independent of CORS; that is a separate issue and was not pursued.

The /plugins Static mount serves fo.config.plugins_dir with follow_symlink=True (fiftyone/server/app.py:149-158); a symlink inside that directory would expose files outside it - outside this advisory, not pursued.
unverified: The supplied fix diff contains no hunks: scr-5041.fix.diff:1-2 is only the merge-commit header ('Merge commit from fork'), so the published fix's exact hunks, the third of the three source files reported by the candidate metadata (c_fix_sites=3, c_site_files=3, c_far_apart=1, c_restructured=1), and its added/changed tests could not be read. fix_sites therefore lists only the two wildcard emissions verified in the pinned tree; the third file is plausibly a shared helper (fiftyone/server/utils/http.py is the natural home and is already imported by fiftyone/server/utils/__init__.py:20) or the launch flags in fiftyone/server/main.py:35-64 / fiftyone/core/service.py:342-354, but this is inference, not evidence.
